text:
Maya S: Heads-up — p95 latency between rack-us-east-3a (gpu12-19) and rack-us-east-3b (gpu2-9) is spiking during the 18:30-19:00 batch ramp. Not steady; looks like bursts every 2-4s when batch size grows. RX errors and fragments tick up. :eyes:

Sahil P: Any recent TOR or MTU changes pushed to those racks? Could be a jumbo mismatch or a QoS bump.

Maya S: Not from infra config side that I can see in the last 24h. Saw a change to trunking on tor-3b at 2025-11-09T02:10Z but engineers said it was a small vlan cleanup.

Ryan L: Running quick checks now. ping/trace for a slow pair:
```
# ping -M do -s 8972 gpu12.rack3a -> gpu4.rack3b
PING ...: frag needed, mtu=1500
# ip -s link show eth1
RX:  packets  txerrors: 98  rxerrors: 104  dropped: 0
```

Katie: infra-bot reported inter-rack alerts earlier? @infra-bot any context? :face_with_monocle:

infra-bot: [ALERT] inter-rack latency spike detected between rack-us-east-3a and rack-us-east-3b at 2025-11-09T18:31:02Z. p95 increased from 12ms -> 220ms for 6m. Event ID: IT-20251109-3321.

Sahil P: That ping output looks like path MTU negotiation failing (DF set + icmp frag-needed). Could be some middlebox or TOR clamping to 1500 while hosts expect 9000. Any recent host kernel or driver updates?

Maya S: Not on the host kernel. But we did push a nic firmware update to the rack on 2025-11-08 during a maintenance slot — I'll cross-check. Also seeing RDMA counters for the pair show increased retries:
```
# rdma stat -d mlx5_0
tx_retries: 320  rx_crc_errors: 12  cq_overflows: 0
```

Ryan L: I just ssh'd to tor-3b, checking switch MTU:
```
TOR> show interface all | include mtu
Ethernet1/1 mtu 1500
Ethernet1/2 mtu 9000
```
Looks like a few ports on that spine/TOR got reset to 1500 after the config sync.

Katie: If ports are mixed (9000 <-> 1500) you get ICMP frag-needed frequently and RDMA/GPUDirect will blow up. We should roll back the last config-sync change for tor-3b and reenable jumbo on the affected trunk ports.

Maya S: Agreed. Quick mitigation: can we temporarily steer batch traffic away from the bad pair? I can update scheduler affinity rules for this window.

Sahil P: I'll open a change to restore MTU to 9000 on the affected interfaces — will target a low-risk 5-min window. ETA 12m.

Ryan L: I'll prepare a revert patch for the config-sync and a safe verification script to assert all rack-to-rack trunks are 9000. Suggest `show interface | grep mtu` + `ethtool -k` on hosts.

Maya S: For the immediate window (next 30m) I've pinned heavy batches off rack-us-east-3b. p95 dropped back to ~18ms after steering.

Katie: I created INFRA-4872 and linked the alert + tor diff + host logs. Assigning to @Sahil P for the MTU fix and @Ryan L to validate and close.

Sahil P: On it. Will post once fixed and verified.

Maya S: Thanks. Follow-up: we should add a small health-probe for MTU consistency to the nightly infra checks (quick `ping -M do -s 8972` pairwise). Saves paging on weekend. :+1:

Ryan L: Good call. I'll add the probe and a Grafana panel for path-MTU failures.

infra-bot: [UPDATE] IT-20251109-3321 -> remediation in progress. Change-scheduled for tor-3b MTU restore.

Maya S: Closing thread for now — will reopen if steering doesn't hold. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
